title: Kashmir, 1819
hook: the valley comes under Sikh rule

segments.voice: Yesterday, Multan, the hot city of saints, and your line, multan joins. Today we climb out of the plains into the mountains, and close the week.

Snow on the passes. A lake with houseboats. Fields of saffron, and shawls so fine, the old stories say, that one could be drawn through a ring. That's Kashmir, the valley ringed by mountains north of the Punjab. For a long time it had been ruled from far away, by governors sent from Kabul. Then, as Sikh histories tell it, an army came up the mountain roads from Lahore, dragging its guns behind it.
screen: `SNOW, SAFFRON, SHAWLS.` → `A VALLEY RULED FROM FAR AWAY.` → `AN ARMY FROM LAHORE.`

segments.voice: Start with the road. Getting an army into Kashmir meant hauling men and guns over high passes, and Sikh histories remember that an earlier try had failed. So the second was planned with care. The Maharaja sent his general, Misr Diwan Chand, a Hindu officer who had risen in his service, with Sikh commanders beside him. The army crossed the mountains, met the Afghan governor's forces, and won the valley. Then the change at the top. Kashmir had been held for the kings in Kabul; now its governors were named in Lahore. Histories tell of Kashmir's shawls and saffron reaching the Lahore court, and of the Maharaja's love of fine Kashmiri things. Now the honest part. Ruling a valley is harder than winning one. Some governors sent from Lahore are remembered well, some less so, and Kashmiri memory of these years is mixed. That belongs in the story too. And look back at this week: gold laid on the Harmandir, a river fixed as a border, an army trained by teachers from many lands, a general who held the frontier, a Maharaja who bowed to correction at the Akal Takht, Multan in the heat. Day by day, a city became a country. The valley is where the map reached the snow.
screen: `A HARD ROAD OVER THE PASSES.` · `GOVERNORS NAMED IN LAHORE.` · `WINNING IS EASIER THAN RULING.` · `A WEEK OF A GROWING KINGDOM.` · then, large: `THE VALLEY.`

segments.voice: Picture mountains on every side of you, close and high, snow on their tops, and down where you sit, sheltered green ground and water moving somewhere nearby. Breathe in the cold, clean air, breathe out slowly, and let the mountains hold the week's noise outside. If you pray, you can say Waheguru quietly on each breath out.
Kashmir. The valley of snow, saffron and shawls, won by an army that crossed the passes from Lahore, and governed from there.
Your line: the valley. Winning a place is easier than ruling it well. That's the week, done.

howItsDone: Sikhs meet the Kashmir campaign in histories of Maharaja Ranjit Singh's reign, where it is told as one of the conquests that took the kingdom into the mountains.
